info.title: jev-provider gateway API
info.description:
Jev/System One compatible decision gateway. It translates a bounded Jev request into one structured-output call to a configured upstream provider (Responses API or Messages API) and maps the result back to Jev answers.

Every response, success or error, carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and the same `gw_<16 hex>` request ID in `x-request-id` and `x-typesafe-request-id`.

Gateway limits. These are gateway policy, not official System One limits. The numbers in this document are the gateway defaults; operators can change each one, and `GET /api/system-one/config` reports the values in effect:
- request body: 524288 bytes (`MAX_BODY_BYTES`)
- questions per request: 1..=32 (`MAX_QUESTIONS`)
- Choice options: 1..=255 (`MAX_CHOICE_OPTIONS`)
- Score levels: 1..=10 (`MAX_SCORE_LEVELS`)
- JSON nesting depth of `state`, `instructions` and each criteria value: 32 (`MAX_JSON_DEPTH`)
- meaningful text: 3 words (`MIN_DESCRIPTION_WORDS`, at least 1; see Question and state rules)
- time to receive the request headers and body: 10000 ms (`REQUEST_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`)
- Idempotency-Key retention: 86400 s (`IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS`), about 100000 entries per process (`IDEMPOTENCY_MAX_ENTRIES`)

Fixed limits (not configurable): question and option names 1..=128 characters and not blank; `model` 1..=128 characters, not blank, no control characters; `Idempotency-Key` 1..=255 visible ASCII bytes.

Question and state rules. Gateway policy, stricter than the official API: a question or `state` without real text returns `422 invalid_request` with a message naming the question (or `state`) and the rule. Text is counted in units over every object key and string value at any depth: each Han, Hiragana, Katakana or Thai character is one unit, other text counts runs of word characters (like the regex `\w+`), and numbers, booleans and null count nothing. Text is meaningful at `MIN_DESCRIPTION_WORDS` units (default 3).
- Noul: meaningful `instructions`, or `criteria` that is one positive/negative pair with both descriptions meaningful.
- Choice: meaningful `instructions`, or a meaningful description for every option.
- Score: meaningful `instructions`, or a meaningful description for every level.
- `state`: not `null`, a number, a boolean, or an array holding only those (at any depth), and at least `MIN_DESCRIPTION_WORDS` units.

The gateway does not count tokens; the upstream provider's own limits apply.

tags.name: Gateway
tags.description: Gateway extensions with no official System One counterpart.

/v1/systemone.description: Any method other than POST returns `405 method_not_allowed` with `"detail": "Method Not Allowed"` and `Allow: POST` (see `components.responses.MethodNotAllowed`). This is the only route that answers 405.

post.summary: Evaluate typed questions against caller state
post.description: Checks run in this order: authentication (401/403), `Content-Type` (415), a declared `Content-Length` over the body limit (413), `Idempotency-Key` syntax (422), body read (408, 413), JSON parsing (400), the Jev contract and its bounds (422), the idempotency cache (409), then the upstream call. A failed upstream attempt is retried up to the provider's `max_retries` (at most 3) for retryable statuses; the caller sees the last error.

requestBody.description: `Content-Type` must start with `application/json` (any case; parameters such as `charset` are allowed). The body must be UTF-8 JSON without duplicate object keys, at most 524288 bytes by default (`MAX_BODY_BYTES`, configurable).

get.description: Gateway extension. No authentication, even when `GATEWAY_API_KEYS` is set: the document is static apart from `info.version` and contains no secrets or configured values. Limits shown are gateway defaults.

gatewayBearer.description: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Required on `POST /v1/systemone` and `GET /v1/models` only when the gateway is configured with `GATEWAY_API_KEYS`; otherwise the header is ignored. The scheme name is case-insensitive (RFC 7235), so `bearer <key>` also works. A missing header, another scheme (such as `Basic`), or an empty token returns `403` with message `Must supply an API key! Check your request and try again.`; a well-formed Bearer token that is not configured returns `401` with message `Cannot authenticate with the server. Please check your API key and try again.`. Both use `error.code` `invalid_api_key` and `detail.error_type` `authentication_error`. The key also scopes the idempotency cache.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Gateway extension. 1..=255 visible ASCII bytes (0x21-0x7E); otherwise `422 invalid_idempotency_key`. Scoped to the caller's gateway key, kept in a process-local cache for `IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS` (default 86400). The same key with the same body bytes replays the cached 200; with a different body it returns `409 idempotency_conflict`; while the first request runs it returns `409 request_in_progress` with `retry-after: 1`; after the first request failed it returns `409 idempotency_failed`. Use a new key for each logical retry.

XRequestId.description: Gateway request ID, `gw_` followed by 16 lowercase hex digits. On every response.

XTypesafeRequestId.description: Same value as `x-request-id`. On every response.

ResponseMode.description: Gateway extension. Provider type that produced the answers: `responses-adapted` (Responses API) or `messages-adapted` (Messages API). Successful decisions only.

IdempotencyReplayed.description: Gateway extension. `true` when the body was replayed from the idempotency cache; absent otherwise.

UpstreamProvider.description: Gateway extension, off by default. Provider registry name. Sent only when `EXPOSE_UPSTREAM_HEADERS=true`.

UpstreamModel.description: Gateway extension, off by default. Upstream model ID. Sent only when `EXPOSE_UPSTREAM_HEADERS=true`.

UpstreamRequestId.description: Gateway extension, off by default. Upstream request ID (from the upstream `x-request-id`, `request-id` or `x-typesafe-request-id` header). Sent only when `EXPOSE_UPSTREAM_HEADERS=true` and the upstream returned one.

ErrorSource.description: Gateway extension. `platform` for errors the gateway raised itself, `upstream` for errors caused by the upstream provider (unreachable, timed out, non-2xx status, refusal, truncated output).

RetryAfter.description: `1` on `409 request_in_progress`. On errors mapped from an upstream non-2xx status, the upstream `retry-after` value when it sent one.

BadRequest.description: `invalid_json`: the body is not UTF-8 JSON, contains duplicate object keys, or failed while being read.

Unauthorized.description: `invalid_api_key`: a well-formed Bearer token that is not configured. Only when `GATEWAY_API_KEYS` is set.

detail.message: Cannot authenticate with the server. Please check your API key and try again.

error.message: Cannot authenticate with the server. Please check your API key and try again.

Forbidden.description: `invalid_api_key`: no `Authorization` header, a non-Bearer scheme, or an empty Bearer token. Only when `GATEWAY_API_KEYS` is set.

detail.message: Must supply an API key! Check your request and try again.

error.message: Must supply an API key! Check your request and try again.

NotFound.description: `not_found`: unknown path, or a method other than GET on a GET route. `detail` is the string `Not Found`.

MethodNotAllowed.description: `method_not_allowed`: a method other than POST on `/v1/systemone`. `detail` is the string `Method Not Allowed`.

RequestTimeout.description: `request_timeout`: the body was not fully received within `REQUEST_READ_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 10000, configurable). A connection that does not send complete request headers in time is closed without a response.

Conflict.description: Idempotency conflicts (only with `Idempotency-Key`): `request_in_progress` (the first request with this key is still running; `retry-after: 1`), `idempotency_conflict` (same key, different body), `idempotency_failed` (the first request with this key failed).

PayloadTooLarge.description: `request_too_large`: the declared `Content-Length` or the bytes received exceed `MAX_BODY_BYTES` (default 524288, configurable).

UnsupportedMediaType.description: `unsupported_media_type`: `Content-Type` is missing or does not start with `application/json`.

UnprocessableEntity.description: `invalid_request`: the JSON does not match the Jev contract, breaks a bound, fails the question and state rules (see the API description), or names an unknown `model` alias. `invalid_idempotency_key`: malformed `Idempotency-Key`. `provider_refused` (source `upstream`): the upstream returned 200 with a refusal; not retried.

TooManyRequests.description: `provider_busy` (source `upstream`): the upstream returned 429. The upstream `retry-after` is forwarded when present.

InternalServerError.description: `internal_error`: the gateway failed to serialize or build a message. `provider_unavailable` (source `upstream`): the upstream returned 500.

BadGateway.description: Source `upstream`: `provider_unavailable` (upstream unreachable, failed mid-response, or returned 502), `provider_rejected_request` (any upstream status other than 429, 529 and 5xx, including 400, 401, 403, 404 and 422; the upstream status appears only in the message and the upstream body is never echoed; not retried), `provider_output_truncated` (upstream 200 cut off at its token limit; not retried). Source `platform`: `invalid_provider_response` (upstream 200 with unusable output: not JSON, no text, wrong shape, or over `MAX_UPSTREAM_BYTES`, default 1048576).

ServiceUnavailable.description: Source `platform`: `provider_busy` (no provider concurrency permit within `ADMISSION_WAIT_MS`, default 5), `provider_not_configured` (the route's provider is not configured), `provider_unavailable` (admission closed). Source `upstream`: `provider_unavailable` (the upstream returned 503).

GatewayTimeout.description: Source `upstream`: `provider_timeout` (an attempt exceeded the provider's `timeout_ms`; default 20000 for `responses-api`, 60000 for `messages-api`) or `provider_unavailable` (the upstream returned 504).

UpstreamServerError.description: Source `upstream`: any other upstream 5xx status keeps its status with `provider_unavailable`; upstream 529 keeps its status with `provider_busy`. The upstream `retry-after` is forwarded when present.

AnyJson.description: Any JSON value. Arrays and objects may nest at most `MAX_JSON_DEPTH` levels (default 32, configurable).

Name.description: Question or option name: 1..=128 characters, not blank (whitespace-only is rejected).

JevRequest.description: Jev decision request. Unknown top-level fields are ignored.

model.description: Gateway extension: optional. Public model alias; absent or `null` uses `DEFAULT_JEV_MODEL` (default `jev-latest`). 1..=128 characters, not blank, no control characters. An unknown alias returns `422 invalid_request` unless the gateway sets `ALLOW_PASSTHROUGH_MODEL=true`, which sends it to the default provider as an upstream model ID.

state.description: Required. Caller evidence, treated as untrusted data. Gateway policy (stricter than the official API): it must be an object, a string, or an array that holds a string or an object somewhere; `null`, a number, a boolean, or an array of only numbers, booleans and nulls (at any depth, e.g. `[1, true, [2]]`) returns `422 invalid_request`. Its keys and string values must hold at least `MIN_DESCRIPTION_WORDS` text units (default 3), so `""`, `{}`, `[]` and `{"temp": 38.5, "fever": true}` (2 units) are rejected. Nesting depth at most `MAX_JSON_DEPTH` (default 32, configurable).

questions.description: Question name to question. 1..=`MAX_QUESTIONS` entries (default 32, configurable).

user_instructions.description: Gateway extension: optional, closed and typed domain context (`schema/user-instructions.schema.json`). Unknown fields return `422 invalid_request`. Beyond the schema, text fields must not be blank (whitespace-only is rejected). `null` is the same as absent.

Question.description: A typed question, selected by `type`. `instructions` and every criteria value are any JSON value within the depth limit. Each question needs meaningful text: `instructions` of at least `MIN_DESCRIPTION_WORDS` text units (default 3), or descriptions as described for each type. This is gateway policy, stricter than the official API; a question that fails returns `422 invalid_request`.

NoulQuestion.description: Probability that a statement is true. Needs meaningful `instructions` or a positive/negative `criteria` pair with two meaningful descriptions.

criteria.description: Optional: `null`, a string, or one positive/negative pair object. A pair object has exactly two keys, a positive and a negative key from the same row of `x-criteria-pairs` (true/false, yes/no, agree/disagree, accept/reject, approve/deny, allow/block, pass/fail, positive/negative), matched case-insensitively; each value is that answer's description. With meaningful `instructions` the pair descriptions may be anything (even empty), and a string is passed to the model as context. Without meaningful `instructions`, `criteria` must be a pair whose two descriptions each have at least `MIN_DESCRIPTION_WORDS` units; a string is then rejected. Other objects (wrong keys, keys from two rows, extra keys), arrays, numbers and booleans return `422 invalid_request`. The model sees a pair as `{"true": <positive>, "false": <negative>}` and returns P(true).

Option name to its description (any JSON value). 1..=`MAX_CHOICE_OPTIONS` options (default 255, configurable). Without meaningful `instructions`, every description needs at least `MIN_DESCRIPTION_WORDS` text units; with them, descriptions are optional (`""` or `null` is fine). Option names are shown to the model and carry meaning.

ScoreQuestion.description: Probability distribution over ordered levels; level `i` is `criteria[i]`.

criteria.description: Level descriptions (any JSON values), lowest first. 1..=`MAX_SCORE_LEVELS` levels (default 10, configurable). Without meaningful `instructions`, every level needs at least `MIN_DESCRIPTION_WORDS` text units; with them, descriptions are optional. With one level the answer is `score` 0, `confidence` 1 and probability 1, as TypeSafe does.

JevResponse.description: Decision result. Keys serialize in a fixed order: top-level `model`, `answers`, `usage`; `answers` in the order the questions appear in the request body; within each answer the official field order (Noul `type`, `noul`; Choice `type`, `choice`, `confidence`, `probabilities`; Score `type`, `score`, `confidence`, `legend`, `probabilities`).

model.description: The route's `response_model` when configured, otherwise the public alias that served the request.

answers.description: One answer per request question, keyed by the caller's question name, in request order.

Answer.description: Answer of the same `type` as its question. Every number (`noul`, `score`, probabilities, `confidence`) is rounded to 2 decimal places, as TypeSafe does. `score`, `confidence` and `choice` are computed from the normalized probabilities before rounding, so the rounded probabilities need not sum to exactly 1.

noul.description: Probability that the statement is true.

choice.description: Option with the highest probability, compared before rounding; on an exact tie, the smallest name in byte order.

probabilities.description: Every declared option name to its probability, normalized to sum to 1 before rounding. Keys in the order the options appear in the request's `criteria`.

confidence.description: `(p_max - 1/n) / (1 - 1/n)` for `n` options; 1 when there is a single option.

score.description: Expected level, `sum(i * p_i)`, between 0 and n-1, rounded to 2 decimals.

probabilities.description: Level index (`"0"`..`"n-1"`) to probability, normalized to sum to 1 before rounding. Keys in numeric order (`"10"` follows `"9"`).

confidence.description: `max(0, 1 - MAD_m / MAD_unif)`: `MAD_m` is the mean absolute level distance from the most likely level (the first maximum in level order), `MAD_unif` the uniform distribution's mean absolute deviation from the center level; 1 when there is a single level.

legend.description: Level index (`"0"`..`"n-1"`) to the caller's `criteria[i]` value, unchanged. Keys in numeric order.

Usage.description: Upstream token counts. Always present; a count the upstream did not report is `null`.

name.description: Public alias, usable as the request `model`.

description.description: From the route; default empty string.

release_date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` from the route; defaults to the gateway release date.

ErrorBody.description: Error envelope. `detail` follows the official System One shape; `error` and `request_id` are gateway extensions.

error_type.description: `authentication_error` for `invalid_api_key`; otherwise the same value as `error.code`.

message.description: Human-readable; never contains upstream error bodies or secrets.

ErrorCode.description: Gateway error code, also sent in `X-System-One-Error-Code`. See the per-status responses for when each occurs.
